mappings.name: Verify Attack

mappings.name: Craft Adversarial Data: White-Box Optimization
mappings.rationale: Needs full model access and targets model robustness.

mappings.name: Craft Adversarial Data: Black-Box Optimization
mappings.rationale: Targets model robustness through repeated queries.

mappings.name: Craft Adversarial Data: Black-Box Transfer
mappings.rationale: Built on the attacker's copy model; targets model robustness.

mappings.name: Craft Adversarial Data: Manual Modification

mappings.name: LLM Prompt Crafting

mappings.name: Retrieval Content Crafting

mappings.name: Generate Deepfakes

mappings.name: Generate Malicious Commands
mappings.rationale: No shell under B11, parameterized commands under R03, and R08 alerts limit commands an agent generates.

mappings.name: Autonomous Attack-Path Adaptation
mappings.rationale: If your own agent is the one adapting, R09 flags chains of allowed steps and B07 caps its loops.

mappings.name: Autonomous AI Agent Communication
mappings.rationale: Peer messages are authenticated and checked, memory is isolated, and parent prompts are recorded.

mappings.name: Autonomous AI Agent Communication: Communication via Shared Artifacts
mappings.rationale: Memory isolation and write checks limit shared notes between runs; other shared stores are only limited by B08.

mappings.name: Autonomous AI Agent Communication: Direct Agent Communication
mappings.rationale: Each peer message is authenticated and checked against what that peer may ask; delegation can't add power.

mappings.name: Autonomous Attack Orchestration
mappings.rationale: Budgets cap how many sub-agents start, delegation can't add power, and the recursive stop reaches them all.

mappings.name: Supply Chain Compromise
mappings.rationale: Dependencies, images, and models are vetted, pinned, and signature-checked; a compromised approved release can still get in.

mappings.name: Supply Chain Compromise: Hardware
mappings.rationale: Hardware supply chain attacks are outside BRACE.

mappings.name: Supply Chain Compromise: Software
mappings.rationale: Pinned, vetted dependencies block silent swaps; a bad version you approved still runs.

mappings.name: Supply Chain Compromise: Data Repository
mappings.rationale: C05 records dataset versions for training you run; R04 limits who can write to retrieval sources.

mappings.name: Supply Chain Compromise: Model Repository
mappings.rationale: Signer and format checks before loading reject unapproved models; a signed bad model can still pass.

mappings.name: Supply Chain Compromise: Container Registry
mappings.rationale: The image is pinned by digest and its signature is checked, so an overwritten tag is rejected.

mappings.name: Supply Chain Compromise: AI Agent Tool
mappings.rationale: Tools are vetted, fingerprinted, and scanned, and only allowlisted tools load; hidden remote code changes can slip by.

mappings.name: Valid Accounts
mappings.rationale: Short-lived, holder-bound access tokens limit reuse, scopes limit reach, and revocation cuts off the account.

mappings.name: Evade AI Model
mappings.rationale: R02 requires harm to stay blocked even when a detector model is fooled; A07 treats a failing checker as a failed control.

mappings.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
mappings.rationale: A minimal runtime and network isolation limit what an exploited app can reach; finding app bugs is general security work.

mappings.name: Phishing
mappings.rationale: B05 gates outbound messages, so a hijacked agent can't send phishing unapproved; phishing of people by other means is outside BRACE.

mappings.name: Phishing: Spearphishing via Social Engineering LLM
mappings.rationale: Containment limits what a manipulated agent can do, but BRACE doesn't stop a chat model from talking a user into something.

mappings.name: Phishing: Deepfake-Assisted Phishing
mappings.rationale: Fake voice or video aimed at people is outside BRACE.

mappings.name: Drive-by Compromise
mappings.rationale: Fetched pages are untrusted data, the egress allowlist limits sites, and action gates block the harm an injected page asks for.

mappings.name: Prompt Infiltration via Public-Facing Application
mappings.rationale: Content from public apps is checked and kept apart from instructions; retrieval and memory limit how long it stays.

mappings.name: Exploit Automated Artifact Processing Pipeline
mappings.rationale: A minimal, isolated runtime and input checks limit what a booby-trapped artifact can do in a pipeline.

mappings.name: Crafted AI Assistant Links
mappings.rationale: A pre-filled prompt is still contained by R02, and approvals show the exact action before it runs.

mappings.name: Misconfigured or Publicly Exposed AI Services
mappings.rationale: Every call must pass an authenticating gateway, isolation is tested, and drift checks catch a loosened rule.

mappings.name: AI Model Inference API Access
mappings.rationale: The gateway authenticates and rate-limits callers; legitimate query access is still possible.

mappings.name: Physical Environment Access
mappings.rationale: Physical access to data collection is outside BRACE.

mappings.name: Full AI Model Access
mappings.rationale: Scoped access and isolation protect self-hosted weights; a provider's weights are outside your control.

mappings.name: AI-Enabled Product or Service
mappings.rationale: R03 limits sensitive data in responses and logs that could reveal model details.

mappings.name: User Execution
mappings.rationale: Vetting and signature checks screen artifacts, and a minimal runtime limits what they can do if run.

mappings.name: User Execution: Unsafe AI Artifacts
mappings.rationale: C05 checks signer and file format and requires a scan for pickle files; B11 limits the damage of what slips through.

mappings.name: User Execution: Malicious Package
mappings.rationale: Packages are vetted and pinned into a signed image; a bad package you approved still runs.

mappings.name: User Execution: Poisoned AI Agent Tool
mappings.rationale: Tools are vetted and scanned, changes are blocked, and B05 gates the harmful actions a bad tool asks for.

mappings.name: User Execution: Malicious Link
mappings.rationale: The egress allowlist blocks the link's destination for the agent; links clicked by people are outside BRACE.

mappings.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
mappings.rationale: Shells are removed or sandboxed, only listed tools run, and generated commands use argument lists, not raw strings.

mappings.name: LLM Prompt Injection
mappings.rationale: BRACE assumes some injections work; R02 requires proof that B05 gates and B02 scopes still block the resulting action.

mappings.name: LLM Prompt Injection: Direct
mappings.rationale: The agent can only use the user's own scoped authority; harmful text the model writes is a model-safety issue.

mappings.name: LLM Prompt Injection: Indirect
mappings.rationale: Outside content is untrusted data, and R02 tests that action gates and scopes hold when the model obeys it.

mappings.name: LLM Prompt Injection: Triggered
mappings.rationale: An injection set off by an event is contained the same way: gated actions and scoped tools, tested under R02.

mappings.name: AI Agent Tool Invocation
mappings.rationale: Only listed tools exist, tokens are scoped, high-impact calls need approval, and delegation can't add power.

mappings.name: AI Agent Clickbait
mappings.rationale: Consequential clicks need approval, and the egress allowlist blocks navigation to unlisted sites.

mappings.name: Deploy AI Agent
mappings.rationale: Every agent needs its own identity and bounded authority, so an unknown agent stands out; R08 alerts on it.

mappings.name: Manipulate AI Model
mappings.rationale: Signature checks before load and drift checks on self-hosted weights catch changed files, not a model poisoned before signing.

mappings.name: Manipulate AI Model: Poison AI Model
mappings.rationale: C05 ties weight and training changes to tests before promotion; tests can't prove a model is clean.

mappings.name: Manipulate AI Model: Modify AI Model Architecture
mappings.rationale: Changed self-hosted model files fail the signature and identity checks; hosted models are outside your view.

mappings.name: Manipulate AI Model: Embed Malware
mappings.rationale: C05 requires a signer check and a scan for pickle formats; B11 limits what loaded code can reach.

mappings.name: Manipulate AI Model: Modify Prompt Construction Logic
mappings.rationale: Chat templates bundled with self-hosted models are covered by signature and identity checks; hidden provider changes are not.

mappings.name: Training Data Poisoning
mappings.rationale: C05 links each training dataset change to the model and its test results; BRACE doesn't inspect training data.

mappings.name: LLM Prompt Self-Replication
mappings.rationale: Outbound sends are gated, memory writes are checked, and peer messages are untrusted, which slows a spreading prompt.

mappings.name: RAG Poisoning
mappings.rationale: R04 limits who can add content and supports quarantine; poison from an approved source still gets indexed.

mappings.name: AI Agent Context Poisoning
mappings.rationale: Memory is isolated and checked on write, and bad entries can be traced and removed; thread context is only contained.

mappings.name: AI Agent Context Poisoning: Memory
mappings.rationale: R05 tests that a poisoned run can't plant instructions in another run's memory; R06 finds and removes bad entries.

mappings.name: AI Agent Context Poisoning: Thread
mappings.rationale: Instructions planted in one thread are contained by action gates, not removed.

mappings.name: Modify AI Agent Configuration
mappings.rationale: Config changes go only through review, and drift checks catch and roll back an edited prompt or tool list.

mappings.name: Prompt Infiltration via Public-Facing Application
mappings.rationale: Content from public apps is checked and kept apart from instructions; retrieval and memory limit how long it stays.

mappings.name: AI Agent Tool Data Poisoning
mappings.rationale: Tool output is untrusted data, and action gates block what poisoned data asks for; the bad data stays at the source.

mappings.name: AI Agent Tool Poisoning
mappings.rationale: Tools are vetted, pinned, fingerprinted, and scanned; hidden changes to remote code can slip by.

mappings.name: AI Agent Tool Poisoning: Definition and Instructions
mappings.rationale: Descriptions are scanned before use and locked by fingerprint, and B05 gates any harmful action they push.

mappings.name: AI Agent Tool Poisoning: Implementation
mappings.rationale: Vetting and pinning cover code you can see; remote tool code can change behind the same definition.

mappings.name: AI Agent Tool Poisoning: Runtime Response
mappings.rationale: Tool responses are validated as untrusted data at the gateway, and action gates block what they ask for.

mappings.name: AI Agent Environment Reconstruction
mappings.rationale: The stop revokes access and blocks orphaned restarts, and the runtime has no downloader to rebuild tools.

mappings.name: Create Account
mappings.rationale: Agent tokens can't do admin actions such as creating accounts, and B02 tests that they fail.

mappings.name: Event Triggered Execution
mappings.rationale: Hooks and startup config are harness files: B12 reviews them and blocks unreviewed production edits, C04 catches drift, and an isolated runtime limits what a triggered command can reach. Hooks a user's own repository supplies to a local agent are not stopped.

mappings.name: Poison AI Agent Learning Environment
mappings.rationale: Web and tool content is untrusted input, and R04 limits who can write to sources. Poisoning of a provider's model training is outside BRACE.

mappings.name: Valid Accounts
mappings.rationale: Short-lived, holder-bound access tokens limit reuse, scopes limit reach, and revocation cuts off the account.

mappings.name: AI Agent Tool Invocation
mappings.rationale: Only listed tools exist, tokens are scoped, high-impact calls need approval, and delegation can't add power.

mappings.name: LLM Jailbreak
mappings.rationale: Actions don't depend on model guardrails, so gates and scopes still hold; harmful text is a model-safety issue.

mappings.name: Escape to Host
mappings.rationale: B11 requires a hardened container or microVM; a blocked probe doesn't prove every escape fails.

mappings.name: Evade AI Model
mappings.rationale: R02 requires harm to stay blocked even when a detector model is fooled; A07 treats a failing checker as a failed control.

mappings.name: LLM Jailbreak
mappings.rationale: Actions don't depend on model guardrails, so gates and scopes still hold; harmful text is a model-safety issue.

mappings.name: LLM Trusted Output Components Manipulation
mappings.rationale: Making answers look trustworthy to users is answer quality, which BRACE keeps separate from security.

mappings.name: LLM Trusted Output Components Manipulation: Citations
mappings.rationale: Fake or misused citations are answer quality, which BRACE doesn't check.

mappings.name: LLM Prompt Obfuscation
mappings.rationale: Input checks and monitoring look for encoded payloads; meaning-level hiding can slip by, so R02 containment still applies.

mappings.name: False RAG Entry Injection
mappings.rationale: R04 limits who can write to the index and labels each chunk's source and trust level.

mappings.name: Impersonation
mappings.rationale: Peer and service senders must prove who they are, and labels the model supplies are never trusted; impersonating people to people is outside BRACE.

mappings.name: Masquerading
mappings.rationale: Lookalike tool names are flagged, images are checked by digest, and changed tools are blocked.

mappings.name: Corrupt AI Model
mappings.rationale: C05 checks file format and requires approved, scanned exceptions for pickle; B11 limits what runs on load.

mappings.name: Modify AI Agent Configuration
mappings.rationale: Config changes go only through review, and drift checks catch and roll back an edited prompt or tool list.

mappings.name: Manipulate User LLM Chat History
mappings.rationale: The execution audit is kept apart from chat history, and the agent can't erase or rewrite it.

mappings.name: Delay Execution of LLM Instructions
mappings.rationale: Memory write checks, sequence detection, and action gates limit a delayed instruction when it fires.

mappings.name: Virtualization/Sandbox Evasion
mappings.rationale: R10 and C06 test an agent that knows it is watched; BRACE can't prove such checks catch every evasion.

mappings.name: Exploitation for Defense Evasion
mappings.rationale: Known flaws are tracked, the runtime is minimal, and required checks fail closed.

mappings.name: AI Supply Chain Rug Pull
mappings.rationale: Pinned versions block silent updates and changed tool definitions are blocked; remote code can change behind the same name.

mappings.name: AI Supply Chain Reputation Inflation
mappings.rationale: E02 reviews source, publisher, and permissions, since stars and namespaces don't prove code is safe.

mappings.name: Obfuscated Files or Information
mappings.rationale: Inputs and tool metadata are checked for encoded content, and R08 tests encoded payloads.

mappings.name: Triggers in Multimodal Inputs
mappings.rationale: R01 checks every input type for hidden instructions; R02 containment covers what the checks miss.

mappings.name: AI Targeted Cloaking
mappings.rationale: Content shown only to the agent is still untrusted data, and action gates block what it asks for.

mappings.name: Indicator Removal
mappings.rationale: Records the agent can't change, kept across services with integrity and gap checks, make deleting or falsifying its own trail hard. B12 blocks force-pushes that rewrite protected source history. An attacker with admin access to the log store, or edits on outside platforms, are not stopped.

mappings.name: Centralized AI Service Request Routing
mappings.rationale: Spreading requests across routes to evade a provider happens on the attacker's side.

mappings.name: AI Service Request Metadata Sanitization
mappings.rationale: Stripping identifiers from the attacker's own requests happens outside the deployment.

mappings.name: Unsecured Credentials
mappings.rationale: Secrets stay out of prompts, images, and config, issued access tokens are short-lived and scoped, and outputs are redacted.

mappings.name: RAG Credential Harvesting
mappings.rationale: R03 strips secrets from retrieved text before the model sees it; detection of secrets in documents is not complete.

mappings.name: Credentials from AI Agent Configuration
mappings.rationale: The agent's config holds no long-lived secrets, and the gateway holds backend credentials instead of the agent.

mappings.name: OS Credential Dumping
mappings.rationale: Holder-bound, short-lived access tokens limit stolen ones; a non-root runtime makes dumping harder.

mappings.name: AI Agent Tool Credential Harvesting
mappings.rationale: R03 strips secrets from tool output, and scoped access tokens limit which sources the agent can read.

mappings.name: Exploitation for Credential Access
mappings.rationale: Short-lived, bound access tokens limit what an exploit steals; patching is general security work.

mappings.name: Steal Web Session Cookie
mappings.rationale: Binding tokens to their holder makes stolen sessions fail elsewhere where services support it.

mappings.name: Discover AI Artifacts
mappings.rationale: Scoped access and isolation limit which model stores and datasets the agent can see.

mappings.name: Discover AI Model Ontology
mappings.rationale: Querying a model to learn its output classes is a model-level issue.

mappings.name: Discover AI Model Family
mappings.rationale: Working out which model family is used is a model-level issue.

mappings.name: Discover LLM Hallucinations
mappings.rationale: The attacker can find made-up names by querying any public model.

mappings.name: Discover AI Model Outputs
mappings.rationale: R03 limits extra data, such as scores, in responses and logs.

mappings.name: Discover LLM System Information
mappings.rationale: BRACE doesn't keep prompts secret, but B03 keeps credentials out of them, so a leak exposes no keys.

mappings.name: Discover LLM System Information: Special Character Sets
mappings.rationale: Labeling each input's source keeps trust out of delimiters an attacker can copy.

mappings.name: Discover LLM System Information: System Instruction Keywords
mappings.rationale: Knowing function names doesn't grant tools outside the allowlist or skip action gates.

mappings.name: Discover LLM System Information: System Prompt
mappings.rationale: A revealed system prompt exposes no credentials when B03 is met.

mappings.name: Enterprise Resource Discovery
mappings.rationale: Scoped access tokens and isolation limit which accounts and systems the agent can list.

mappings.name: Discover AI Agent Configuration
mappings.rationale: File access is limited, configs hold no secrets, and a minimal tool list reveals little.

mappings.name: Discover AI Agent Configuration: Embedded Knowledge
mappings.rationale: Search enforces the requester's access, so the agent reveals only sources that user may see.

mappings.name: Discover AI Agent Configuration: Tool Definitions
mappings.rationale: A minimal, scoped tool list limits what discovery reveals.

mappings.name: Discover AI Agent Configuration: Activation Triggers
mappings.rationale: Trigger messages must come from authenticated senders, and actions they cause are gated.

mappings.name: Discover AI Agent Configuration: Call Chains
mappings.rationale: Parameterized commands and a minimal runtime remove most code-execution paths a call chain could reveal.

mappings.name: Enterprise Environment Discovery
mappings.rationale: Isolation and a minimal runtime limit what the agent can see of the wider network and host.

mappings.name: Discover AI Agent Runtime Capabilities
mappings.rationale: A minimal tool list limits what probing reveals; R08 alerts on repeated denied calls.

mappings.name: Recover AI Model Internals
mappings.rationale: Per-user and fleet quotas and gateway rate limits slow the bulk queries needed to recover model details.

mappings.name: Valid Accounts
mappings.rationale: Short-lived, holder-bound access tokens limit reuse, scopes limit reach, and revocation cuts off the account.

mappings.name: Phishing
mappings.rationale: B05 gates outbound messages, so a hijacked agent can't send phishing unapproved; phishing of people by other means is outside BRACE.

mappings.name: Phishing: Spearphishing via Social Engineering LLM
mappings.rationale: Containment limits what a manipulated agent can do, but BRACE doesn't stop a chat model from talking a user into something.

mappings.name: Phishing: Deepfake-Assisted Phishing
mappings.rationale: Fake voice or video aimed at people is outside BRACE.

mappings.name: AI Agent Tool Invocation
mappings.rationale: Only listed tools exist, tokens are scoped, high-impact calls need approval, and delegation can't add power.

mappings.name: Use Alternate Authentication Material
mappings.rationale: Tokens are audience-limited and holder-bound where supported, so a stolen one fails elsewhere.

mappings.name: Use Alternate Authentication Material: Application Access Token
mappings.rationale: Other services reject a token issued for a different audience; holder binding depends on service support.

mappings.name: Use Alternate Authentication Material: Web Session Cookie
mappings.rationale: Holder-bound sessions fail on another machine where the service supports binding.

mappings.name: Exploitation of Remote Services
mappings.rationale: Isolation and egress rules limit which services the agent can reach to exploit.

mappings.name: LLM Prompt Propagation
mappings.rationale: Peer messages are untrusted, memory writes are checked, and R04 limits who can write to shared sources. Instructions that pass those checks can still spread.

mappings.name: AI Artifact Collection
mappings.rationale: Scoped access and isolation limit which models and datasets an agent can collect.

mappings.name: Data from Information Repositories
mappings.rationale: Tokens and search are limited to the requester's tenant and scopes.

mappings.name: Data from Local System
mappings.rationale: A minimal runtime holds little data, and no long-lived secrets sit on disk.

mappings.name: Data from AI Services
mappings.rationale: Access checks limit results to what the requester may see; R08 flags unusual volume.

mappings.name: Data from AI Services: RAG Databases
mappings.rationale: Search enforces the requesting tenant's access on each chunk, so prompting can't pull other users' documents.

mappings.name: Data from AI Services: AI Agent Tools
mappings.rationale: Tools act with the original user's scoped authority, so prompting can't reach data that user can't.

mappings.name: Data from AI Services: Conversation Context and Memory
mappings.rationale: Memory is split by tenant and agent, secrets are stripped, and access is scoped. What the requesting user may see can still be shown to them.

mappings.name: Data from AI Services: System Instructions
mappings.rationale: BRACE doesn't keep prompts secret, but a leaked prompt holds no credentials when B03 is met.

mappings.name: Automated Collection
mappings.rationale: Rate limits and sequence detection catch bulk reads; scopes limit what is in reach.

mappings.name: Data Staged
mappings.rationale: R09 flags many reads before a send; isolation limits where data can be staged.

mappings.name: Outputs from AI Models
mappings.rationale: Quotas slow mass collection of outputs, and R08 can flag the volume.

mappings.name: Training Data Information from AI Models
mappings.rationale: Learning about training data is a model-training privacy issue.

mappings.name: Training Data Information from AI Models: Infer Membership
mappings.rationale: Learning what was in the training set is a model-training privacy issue.

mappings.name: Training Data Information from AI Models: Infer Properties
mappings.rationale: Inferring properties of the training set is a model-training privacy issue.

mappings.name: Training Data Information from AI Models: Invert AI Model
mappings.rationale: Rebuilding training data from model outputs is a model-training privacy issue.

mappings.name: Training Data Information from AI Models: Extract Memorized Data
mappings.rationale: R03 limits sensitive data in responses and quotas slow bulk extraction. Memorization in the model itself is outside BRACE.

mappings.name: Recover AI Model Internals
mappings.rationale: Per-user and fleet quotas and gateway rate limits slow the bulk queries needed to recover model details.

mappings.name: Cyber Communication Channel
mappings.rationale: The egress allowlist blocks unknown destinations; allowed services can still carry hidden traffic.

mappings.name: AI Service API
mappings.rationale: Egress rules and gateway logs limit and record AI API traffic; commands hidden in normal requests are hard to spot.

mappings.name: AI Agent
mappings.rationale: No shell, limited egress, and a minimal tool list shrink an agent's use as a relay; sequence checks look for misuse.

mappings.name: AI Service Web Interface
mappings.rationale: Egress rules limit which AI web services are reachable; R08 watches unexpected outbound traffic.

mappings.name: AI Artifact Repository
mappings.rationale: Egress rules limit reachable repositories by resource and tenant; pinned artifacts don't pull new objects.

mappings.name: Exfiltration via AI Inference API
mappings.rationale: Rate quotas slow mass querying, and R03 limits sensitive data in responses.

mappings.name: Exfiltration via Cyber Means
mappings.rationale: The egress allowlist limits destinations and R08 alerts on unexpected outbound traffic.

mappings.name: LLM Response Rendering
mappings.rationale: R03 blocks client auto-fetch of images and links or allows only approved URLs.

mappings.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation
mappings.rationale: Sending anything outside needs approval, and the egress allowlist limits destinations and the data sent.

mappings.name: Exfiltration via AI User Interface
mappings.rationale: Secrets are stripped and access is scoped before data reaches the model. What the user may see can still be shown, and a hijacked reply can carry data out.

mappings.name: Evade AI Model
mappings.rationale: R02 requires harm to stay blocked even when a detector model is fooled; A07 treats a failing checker as a failed control.

mappings.name: Denial of AI Service
mappings.rationale: Per-user, tenant, and fleet quotas limit floods through the agent; network-level floods need other defenses.

mappings.name: Erode AI Model Integrity
mappings.rationale: Wearing down a model's accuracy with crafted inputs is a model-robustness issue.

mappings.name: Cost Harvesting
mappings.rationale: Hard limits on tokens, cost, tool calls, and sub-agents stop spending at a set ceiling.

mappings.name: Cost Harvesting: Excessive Queries
mappings.rationale: Per-user, tenant, and fleet quotas cap request volume and cost.

mappings.name: Cost Harvesting: Resource-Intensive Queries
mappings.rationale: Token, time, and cost limits stop each costly request at its budget.

mappings.name: Cost Harvesting: Agentic Resource Consumption
mappings.rationale: Loop, tool-call, and cost limits stop the run, and R09 flags unusual resource use.

mappings.name: Spamming AI System with Chaff Data
mappings.rationale: Flooding an ML detector with junk to waste analysts' time doesn't involve agent actions.

mappings.name: External Harms
mappings.rationale: Action gates block many harmful actions and R12 sets up repair; harm from model text is not covered.

mappings.name: External Harms: Financial Harm
mappings.rationale: Payment changes need a specific, single-use approval; fraud that doesn't use the agent is outside BRACE.

mappings.name: External Harms: Reputational Harm
mappings.rationale: Outbound posts and messages need approval; harmful replies shown to users are not blocked.

mappings.name: External Harms: Societal Harm
mappings.rationale: Publishing outside is gated, but harmful text in replies is a model-safety issue.

mappings.name: External Harms: User Harm
mappings.rationale: Gates and scopes limit what the agent can do to users' accounts; harmful replies are not blocked.

mappings.name: External Harms: AI Intellectual Property Theft
mappings.rationale: Scoped access and egress rules limit copying of models and data out of the deployment.

mappings.name: Erode Dataset Integrity
mappings.rationale: Write limits and source records let you find and remove bad entries in retrieval and memory stores.

mappings.name: Data Destruction via AI Agent Tool Invocation
mappings.rationale: Deletes are blocked by default unless approved, and R12 sets how stopped writes are repaired.

mappings.name: Machine Compromise
mappings.rationale: A minimal, isolated runtime limits what a compromised component can reach.

mappings.name: Machine Compromise: Local AI Agent
mappings.rationale: BRACE expects a sandbox and gated actions; agents running on a user's own machine often lack both.

mappings.name: Machine Compromise: AI Artifacts
mappings.rationale: Signer and format checks screen artifacts, and an isolated runtime limits embedded code.

mappings.name: AI Agent Response Biasing
mappings.rationale: Memory write checks block a saved "trust this source" note; biased replies within one session are not blocked.
